bib.title: Cognitive Behaviors that Enable Self-Improving Reasoners, or, Four Habits of Highly Effective STaRs

question: Why do some base language models improve substantially under RL on a verifiable task while others plateau, and which initial properties enable it?
hypothesis: Certain reasoning behaviors (verification, backtracking, subgoal setting, backward chaining) in the initial policy are necessary for efficiently using increased test-time compute through RL.
contributions: Framework of four cognitive behaviors with an LLM classifier to count them in model outputs
Show Qwen-2.5-3B exhibits the behaviors naturally and improves under RL on Countdown while Llama-3.2-3B does not
Priming Llama with synthetic behavior traces (even incorrect ones) enables RL gains matching Qwen
Continued pretraining on behavior-filtered OpenWebMath lets Llama match Qwen's RL trajectory

method.summary: PPO (VERL, TinyZero implementation) on the Countdown game with Qwen-2.5-3B and Llama-3.2-3B base models. Llama is first primed by SFT on Claude-3.5-Sonnet-generated Countdown traces with controlled behaviors, or continued-pretrained on 8.3M tokens of behavior-filtered, rewritten OpenWebMath, then RL-trained; behaviors are counted with a GPT-4o-mini classifier.
method.task: Countdown (arithmetic search puzzle) RL; behavior analysis

datasets.name: Countdown
datasets.size: not stated for RL (batch 256 train / 1312 validation)
datasets.source: Gandhi et al. 2024 / Pan et al. 2025 (TinyZero); numbers and target randomly sampled

datasets.name: Priming SFT datasets (5, Claude-generated)
datasets.size: 1,200 unique Countdown games per dataset; 1000 train / 200 validation
datasets.preprocessing: Two controls: empty CoT '<think></think>' and length-matched placeholder CoT '<think>. . . . . </think>'; also an incorrect-solutions variant of all-strategies

datasets.name: OpenWebMath (curated and behavior-minimized)
datasets.source: OpenWebMath (Paster et al. 2023); classified and rewritten by Qwen-2.5-32B into question-thought-answer XML format, first-person thoughts
datasets.preprocessing: Binary per-document behavior labels from classifier give a behavior-curated set and a behavior-minimized control

datasets.name: OpenWebMath and FineMath (frequency analysis)
datasets.source: Paster et al. 2023; Allal et al. 2025
datasets.preprocessing: Qwen-2.5-32B classifier via vLLM, temperature 0, 1024 generation tokens per behavior

models.name: Llama-3.2-3B
models.context: 2048 in SFT; 256 prompt + 1024 response in RL

other.use: behavior classifier, 4 questions per trajectory, 512 tokens, temperature 0

training.objective: SFT priming (next-token on traces); PPO on Countdown with outcome reward (correct 1.0, incorrect 0.0, correct-format bonus 0.1); continued pretraining on rewritten OpenWebMath
training.optimizer: SFT: AdamW (Loshchilov & Hutter 2019); PPO optimizer not stated
training.lr_schedule: SFT: linear warmup then cosine annealing
training.batch_size: SFT 64 train / 64 validation; PPO 256 train / 1312 validation, PPO mini-batch 128
training.tokens: continued pretraining: 8.3 million tokens per dataset
training.seq_len: SFT context 2048; PPO 256 prompt + 1024 response tokens

other.algorithm_choice: PPO chosen over GRPO/REINFORCE for stability across hyperparameters; performance anecdotally similar

inference.prompting: Countdown prompt format with query/think/answer tags; MATH comparison used 'our prompt format' and Qwen 4-shot format (text not given in PDF)

other.test_time_scaling: token budget 2^7 (128) to 2^10 (1024), checkpoints 0 to 200 PPO steps (App G)

metrics.name: Countdown score
metrics.definition: RL reward-based score on Countdown (correct answer 1.0, format bonus 0.1); plotted as 'score'

metrics.name: Average behavior count
metrics.definition: Average number of distinct occurrences per trajectory of verification, backtracking, subgoal setting, backward chaining, counted by GPT-4o-mini

metrics.name: ICC3
metrics.definition: Intraclass correlation of classifier vs Claude and two humans on 100 trajectories

eval.protocol: Single training curves per condition; no seeds or confidence intervals stated.

limits: Domain is Countdown only for the main causal tests; authors concede priming data was domain-specific and the set of behaviors is not exhaustive.
Only two 3B base model families (plus Llama-70B baseline analysis); no seeds or error bars stated.
Authors say which behaviors matter is likely task-dependent (backtracking and verification mattered most in Countdown) and untested for coding, games, creative writing.
Behavior counts depend on a GPT-4o-mini classifier; agreement with humans on backward chaining is lower (ICC3 0.55 and 0.40).
Curated-pretraining Llama shows no accuracy gain on GPQA (about 12% for both) despite behavior transfer.
Compute, hardware and continued-pretraining hyperparameters are not stated.
